eval-bot: nightly-eval alert for redwood/open-7b-ptq on summarization-prod promptset — ROUGE-L dropped 14% vs baseline (yesterday). flagged: quality_regression.

eval-bot: sample failing generation (truncated):
```
Input: "Summarize the article about municipal budget reallocations."
Model output: "In 2024 the council decided to invest heavily in unrelated projects. The minister declared the old law invalid and replaced it with new directives, leading to several undocumented transfers. For more info, see /random/link which lists all transfers (not authoritative)."
```

alyssa: ugh. this is verbose and hallucinating facts. Did anything land in inference-runtime or model-config last night?

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary deploy 2024-11-08T02:14Z -> inference-runtime v3.2.1 (commit c4f0d2). Changes: default sampling policy: top_p set from 0.7 -> 0.95; tokenizer patch: preserve_special_tokens=true.

marco: that's suspicious — higher top_p + PTQ could increase hallucination risk. i'll run a quick reproduce with sampling pinned.

jasmine: also checked quant-cal logs for the model during PTQ. calibration loss curves look normal, no obvious divergence.

marco: local repro results:
- top_p=0.95 (canary): hallucination rate ~26% on promptset
- top_p=0.7 (baseline): hallucination rate ~7%
- deterministic greedy: hallucination ~5% (for reference)
So default sampling change explains most of the delta.

samir: interesting — could PTQ amplify the effect? quantized logits tend to be less peaked, so sampling with a larger tail (higher top_p) will surface low-prob tokens more often. combined -> more fabricated details.

alyssa: that matches. also saw some outputs with an extra literal token sequence `See /random/link` — that smells like a tokenization shift for URLs after preserve_special_tokens=true. Could be unrelated but worth checking.

jasmine: ran tokenizer diff between v2 and v3 patch. found that URLs now include a leading slash tokenization change: previously "https" tokens kept intact, now broken into ["/","random","/","link"] for some inputs. weird.

samir: plausible chain: tokenizer change -> different token boundaries -> PTQ calibration sees slightly different distribution -> logits softened -> with top_p=0.95 sampling picks unlikely fragments -> hallucinations.

alyssa: proposed immediate mitigations:
1) rollback runtime default sampling to top_p=0.7 for hosted API and halt canary promotion.
2) pin tokenizer config for existing models (set preserve_special_tokens=false) until we validate the new tokenization with PTQ.
3) add gating rule: nightly-eval must not drop ROUGE-L by >5% vs baseline for any promoted model or config change.
4) create canary job that runs full summarization promptset (not just smoke) before promoting config changes.

deploy-bot: initiating rollback to inference-runtime v3.2.0 (commit b9a1e5) for hosted cluster. Canary halted.

opsbot: rollback started (job id 9876). estimated completion 02:32Z. notifying affected customers.

sre-oncall: i'll watch error/latency dashboards during rollback window. ping me if anything spikes.

marco: after rollback i re-ran the reproduce suite (on the same PTQ build). results: top_p at 0.7 -> hallucination rate back to 6.8%. tokenization revert removed the weird slash-token examples.

eval-bot: re-run nightly (manual) completed: ROUGE-L now within +1.8% of baseline. status: regression resolved.

alyssa: root cause summary (for the ticket):
- primary cause: change in inference-runtime default sampling policy (top_p 0.7 -> 0.95) increased headroom for unlikely tokens, leading to more fabricated content in summarization prompts.
- amplifier: tokenizer config change (preserve_special_tokens=true) altered token boundaries for URLs and some short phrases, interacting poorly with PTQ-softened logits.
- PTQ effect: quantization reduced logit sharpness slightly, making sampling-sensitive defaults more impactful.

alyssa: actions (owners + ETA):
- rollback applied (done) — alyssa (owner) — completed 02:35Z 2024-11-08.
- add gating rule to model-config CI: nightly summarization ROUGE-L delta threshold 5% — jasmine (PR by 2024-11-10).
- add targeted canary job that runs summarization promptset on any runtime/config change before promotion — marco (PR + infra job by 2024-11-12).
- update model onboarding checklist to include tokenizer-diff step + PTQ-sampling sensitivity test — samir (doc by 2024-11-14).
- run a small sweep to measure PTQ calibration sensitivity vs tokenization changes — eng-ml (experiment queued, results by 2024-11-18).

marco: i'll also add a quick unit test in serve-config to fail fast if default sampling > 0.8 for production models. small guard.

jasmine: putting patch PRs up for gating and tokenizer pin now -> link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4521

alyssa: nice. can we also log a few representative failing + fixed generation pairs into the regression-runbook so on-call has examples?

opsbot: uploaded artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/2398765432/ (samples + reproduce logs).

eval-bot: adding this thread to ticket RED-2219 (quality regression: summarization promptset).

samir: follow-ups: when we re-enable the tokenizer change, we should run a calibration re-tuning for PTQ and a small generation-distribution test to ensure no metric regressions.

alyssa: agreed. closing loop: regression resolved by rollback; follow-up items assigned. thanks team :heart:
